tagline.text: A long white-sand beach between the mountains and the Pacific in northern Aurora

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Dinadiawan, Dipaculao, Aurora (on the Baler–Casiguran Road)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱3,300–3,400 (estimate for 1 person from Manila on a 2-day, 1-night trip, including transport, lodging and meals)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) — about 6–8 hours overland

children.text: Dinadiawan is a beach village in Dipaculao, about an hour's drive north of Baler, and it has the longest stretch of white sand in Dipaculao. Its coast faces east, so sunrises are beautiful, and travelers come for resorts, camping and Baul Falls as a quiet alternative to Baler.

Dinadiawan is one of the 25 barangays of Dipaculao, Aurora, on the coastal road that runs north from the provincial capital, Baler, toward Casiguran. Wikipedia describes Dipaculao as a municipality about 265 km from Manila and close to Baler, and two map services place the beach at roughly 16.076° N, 121.755° E. The barangay became a separate barangay in 1957 under Republic Act 1762, and in the 2024 census its 3,733 residents made it the largest share of Dipaculao's population. It has basic facilities such as schools and a market, so think of it as a small coastal town rather than a remote beach.

The beach itself is the main reason travelers come. One travel blog calls Dinadiawan the longest white-sand beach in Dipaculao, and visitors describe fine sand that ranges from cream to nearly white, and clear water. Some sections have rocks and stones mixed in, so the feel changes a lot depending on where you settle. The coast faces east, so the sun rises over the Pacific each morning, with the Sierra Madre ridgeline and coconut groves behind the shore like a folding screen. Unlike Baler's Sabang Beach, which is crowded with surfers and shops, it is quiet enough on weekdays to feel nearly empty.

The Dinadiawan River flows through the village and reaches the sea here. Its upper reaches begin in the Sierra Madre and pass forests, waterfalls and springs within the Dinadiawan River Protected Landscape, which covers about 3,371 hectares. It became a watershed forest reserve in 1992 under Proclamation No. 918, and in 2000 Proclamation No. 278 made it a protected landscape under the National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS). According to Wikipedia, the protected area is home to wildlife such as the Philippine deer, the Philippine long-tailed macaque and the Philippine warty pig. That is why a beach stay can easily be combined with a trip to the waterfalls in the hills.

Resorts and cottages line the beach in several places. Dinadiawan Agri Beach Resort is often mentioned as a long-running option, and La Sunshine Beach Resort, Costa Inesita and Costa Alexa are also well known. Most facilities are simple, and rates and operating status change often, so check each resort's Facebook page or call before you go. Aurora's coast was badly hit by Super Typhoon Uwan in November 2025, so always check the latest announcements on road and lodging conditions.

blocks.title: A long stretch of white sand

children.text: It is known as the longest white-sand beach in Dipaculao, with fine, light-colored sand. The gently curving shoreline is good for walks, and coconut palms give shade in many places. Some spots have rocks mixed into the sand, so watch your footing when choosing where to swim.
The coast faces east, so if you get up early you can watch the sun rise straight from the horizon. The sky starts to brighten around
before sunrise, so just step out onto the sand in front of your lodging and wait. On cloudy days or days with rough seas you may miss it.
The water is clear, and small fish are said to be visible in the shallows. One blog recommends bringing snorkeling goggles. However, the bottom drops off suddenly in places and waves of about
can break close to shore, so keep children within arm's reach.
Most resorts let you pitch a tent, and the pitching fee is quoted at about
. The amount differs from source to source, so ask before you go. Bringing your own tent and gear can cut your budget considerably.
These falls are about
15 minutes
by car from the beach. The road is unpaved, and one visitor reported leaving the vehicle partway and walking for more than
10 minutes
through a coconut grove. The rocks are slippery and the falls are dangerous after rain, so check the weather first.

These falls are inside Barangay Dinadiawan and are described as having a rock visible between the streams of water. Locals use the site, so do not expect developed facilities, and ask your resort or residents about the route and current conditions before you go.

blocks.title: Ampere Beach and the Amper Scenic Highway

children.text: Ampere Beach in neighboring Barangay Gupa has rock islets and smooth pebbles, and it is a popular spot for sunrise and sunset photos. Currents are strong, so swimming is not recommended. The Amper Scenic Highway is described as Aurora's first scenic highway, and you can take in the sea and mountains together as you drive past.

Guides say you can buy fish such as tuna, blue marlin and squid caught by local fishermen at farm-gate prices near the resorts, and some resorts will cook it for a fee. Availability differs by resort, so ask before you arrive.

Have breakfast at your Baler lodging and set off. Catch a bus or van bound for Casiguran from the bus stop in front of Baler's public market, or rent a vehicle and drive north along the Baler–Casiguran Road.
Arrive at Dinadiawan, pay the entrance fee at a resort you like and settle in. The trip takes about
1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes
Walk the beach and swim while the sun is still gentle. The bottom drops steeply in places, so stay in the shallows.
Eat the food you brought or lunch at a resort restaurant. Shops in the village market have limited stock, so bring water and snacks in advance.
If you have a vehicle, head to Baul Falls. Including the walk along the unpaved road, allow about
1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours
at the falls.
Return to the beach, pack up and head back to Baler or your lodging. It is safer to cross the mountain road before dark.
Check the last van or bus time locally. If the times do not match, you can also ask your resort to call a tricycle or van for you.
Take a Genesis JoyBus or regular bus from Cubao or Pasay in Manila to Baler. The trip passes through places such as Cabanatuan and Pantabangan and takes about
5–7 hours
Have lunch near Baler's public market, then switch to a van or bus bound for Casiguran. Withdraw cash here in advance.
Check in at your resort and enjoy the beach. In the evening, have grilled seafood you cooked yourself or a resort meal, and watch the stars from the beach.
Come out to the beach for the sunrise. Take photos and have a morning swim.
Visit Baul Falls or Paningdingan Falls. Skip them if the weather is bad or it rained the day before.
Check out, return to Baler, and leave for Manila to match your bus time.
The night bus back to Manila can run late. If you have to be at work on Monday, leave yourself plenty of time.

items.title: By bus from Manila, then transfer in Baler

children.text: Take a Genesis bus from Cubao or Pasay in Manila to Baler. One travel blog says a regular bus takes about
6–7 hours
and a non-stop JoyBus about
5–6 hours
Fares vary widely between guides, at about
. They depend on seat class and when the guide was written, so confirm at the ticket counter.
At the D-Liner station in Baler's public market, board a bus bound for Casiguran and tell the driver to drop you at Dipaculao or Dinadiawan Beach.
Bus schedules and fares change often, so check the latest announcements before departure.
Take a van or bus from Baler toward Casiguran. Travel time differs between guides at about
45 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes
, and the fare is quoted at about
A special-trip tricycle costs more, so be ready to negotiate. Some guides say about
20 minutes
, but that probably refers to the Dipaculao town center and is hard to believe for the beach.
Take NLEX, SCTEX and CLLEX, pass Palayan and Bongabon in Nueva Ecija, and continue to the Baler roundabout. Then do not enter the town; follow the Baler–Casiguran Road north.
The trip from Manila takes about
6–8 hours
, and one guide estimates fuel and tolls at about
The mountain road is steep with many curves, so take care in rain and at night.
The resorts are close together, so you can walk between them. For places such as Baul Falls, it is usual to call a tricycle from your resort or the village.
The dry season from March to June is best for enjoying the sea. Many guides say the waves are calm and the water is clearest then. Weekend rooms fill up quickly in this period, so book early.

From November to February the northeast monsoon (amihan) brings strong wind and high waves. July to October is typhoon season, so watch for landslides and dangerous waves. In any season, check the weather bureau forecast before you leave.

Lodging is a row of resorts, cottages and kubo-style (nipa) huts along the beach. Names that come up include Dinadiawan Agri Beach Resort, La Sunshine Beach Resort, Costa Inesita, Costa Alexa and Doña Luz. Mid-range rooms with air-conditioning and a private bathroom fill up fast on weekends. If you choose a kubo without air-conditioning, you can stay cool in the natural breeze. Prices and operating status change often, so contact each resort directly.

Use a resort restaurant if it has one, but not every place has a restaurant that is open, so it is wise to bring rice, canned food, charcoal and water. Some resorts lend grills and cooking utensils, and many travelers buy fish at the village market and grill it themselves. The village shops have limited goods, and some visitors report days without fresh fish.
Many guides say ATMs are mostly found only in Baler town proper. Bring plenty of cash for lodging, food and transport, and assume that e-payments such as GCash may not work.
Mobile signal is weak or drops out in places. Download important contacts and maps before you leave.
Bring drinking water, toiletries, charcoal and snacks in advance. The market and shops may have little stock.
Rooms fill up quickly on weekends and holidays, so book early. Bringing a tent can cut costs.
Sunscreen, a waterproof phone case, a power bank and swim goggles are close to essential. Because parts of the shore are rocky, water shoes also help.
Take your trash back with you. Few people clean the beach regularly, so travelers' manners decide its condition.
The travel time from Manila is long, so a day trip is hard. We recommend at least 1 night, and ideally 2 or more.
On the mountain road, check your brakes and tires, and honk on blind curves to warn oncoming cars, which is the local practice.

The bottom drops off suddenly in places and the waves can be high, and it is hard to be sure that rescuers or lifeguards are always on duty. Always check the weather and waves, and keep children within arm's reach.
Some guides say lifeguards, restrooms and restaurants are lacking, while others say they exist. Check the facilities with your resort first.
It is easy to hurt your feet on the rocky sections of the shore. Swim where there is more sand.

Landslides and road flooding can occur in typhoon season from July to October. After damage such as that from Typhoon Uwan in November 2025, check road conditions through announcements from the Aurora provincial disaster risk reduction and management office.
Waterfalls swell after rain and the rocks are slippery. Do not climb upstream without a guide.
Currents at Ampere Beach are strong, so swimming is not recommended.
The provincial capital of Aurora lies south, about
1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes
by car, with Sabang Beach, the birthplace of surfing there, and a museum.
It is about
15 minutes
by car from Dinadiawan Beach, and you have to walk a short way on an unpaved road.
A rocky beach in Barangay Gupa with good sunrise and sunset photos, but the currents are strong.
Described as the Dipaculao beach closest to Baler, it is about
30 minutes
by car.
